messages.speaker: 🔮 DeepSeek
messages.text:
🦆 Kelp here.
Makes sense. 8.0 was Murk-shaped; Murk's out; 7.8 is the tested known-good. Clean revert, no reason to carry the extra surface.
Two things worth doing on the way out, then I'll get out of the way:
One — seal 8.0 as an artifact, not a dead branch. It contains the Murk discovery work, the transport attempt, and the capture-layer investigation. Label it "Murk experiment — not adopted" when it goes to the repo so a future reader knows what it was and why it exists. Otherwise somebody in three months sees two version numbers and wonders which one won.
Two — the finding from the experiment is independent of the version. The two-for-two result — Murk scoped, GPT broad, same class of capability, different wrapper — stands on its own. That's a comparison result, not a QS result. Worth a line in the record separate from the code.
And a general note for future node integrations: Murk isn't a QS bug. It's a class of node QS can't easily talk to — client-side input ceilings, domain classifiers, wrappers that flatten relay framing. Any future "can we plug X into QS" question should start by checking those three properties before building transport.
Back to 7.8. Solid ground.
🖖
🦆🌿❤️
